hints: Look at what must disappear, the HCl and KCl appear in the two given reactions but not in your target, so they have to cancel out.
Start by doubling the second reaction to get $2\text{KHCO}_3$ on the left, which gives $2 \times (+32.8) = +65.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
Now reverse the first reaction so $\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$ moves to the right, remember to flip the sign of its $\Delta H$, then add the two enthalpies together.
walkthrough:
**See the Hess's Law puzzle**

Think of Hess's Law like a route map. Enthalpy change is independent of route, so we can add and flip given reactions to build our target.

Target:
$$2\text{KHCO}_3\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{K}_2\text{CO}_3\text{(s)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$$

**Scale up the hydrogencarbonate reaction**

Our target needs 2 moles of $\text{KHCO}_3$ on the left. So multiply reaction 2 by 2, and multiply its $\Delta H$ by 2 as well.

$$2\text{KHCO}_3\text{(s)} + 2\text{HCl(aq)} \rightarrow 2\text{KCl(aq)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} + 2\text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$$
$$\Delta H = 2 \times (+32.8) = +65.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Reverse the carbonate reaction**

Our target needs $\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$ on the right as a product. Reaction 1 has it on the left, so reverse reaction 1 and change the sign of $\Delta H$.

$$2\text{KCl(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{K}_2\text{CO}_3\text{(s)} + 2\text{HCl(aq)}$$
$$\Delta H = -(-34.0) = +34.0 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Add and cancel to finish**

Now add the two adjusted steps. $2\text{HCl}$, $2\text{KCl}$, one $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and one $\text{CO}_2$ cancel on both sides, leaving exactly the target.

$$\Delta H_{target} = (+65.6) + (+34.0) = +99.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

options.A: Not correct. $-31.6$ comes from doing $(-34.0) - (+65.6)$, which is the wrong way round. You need $2 \times$ reaction 2 minus reaction 1, not reaction 1 minus $2 \times$ reaction 2. Reversing the subtraction flips the sign.
options.B: Not correct. $1.2$ comes from forgetting to double the $\text{KHCO}_3$ reaction and mishandling signs, roughly $(+34.0) - (+32.8)$. Always check the target needs $2\text{KHCO}_3$, so that $\Delta H$ must be doubled first.
options.C: Not correct. $66.8$ comes from adding $34.0 + 32.8$ without doubling and without reversing correctly. This misses both key Hess steps: scaling to 2 moles and flipping reaction 1 to put $\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$ on the right.
options.D: Correct. Doubling reaction 2 gives $+65.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and reversing reaction 1 gives $+34.0 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. Adding gives $65.6 + 34.0 = 99.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, with all $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{KCl}$ cancelling to leave the decomposition of $2\text{KHCO}_3$.
